title: "When Experience Meets Environment: Professional Backgrounds, Court Composition, and Decision-Making in Immigration Court"
sort: 1
author:
  - name: Sara Heridia
  - name: Matthew Martin
categories:

pub-info:
  status: "Under review"
  abstract: >-
    Research on judicial behavior shows that professional backgrounds shape how judges decide but often assumes the effect is uniform across institutional settings. Focusing on U.S. immigration courts, we argue that the influence of professional experience depends on the specificity of prior socialization and the court in which a judge sits. Analyzing over 550,000 decisions by 502 judges in 67 courts (2015--2018), we disaggregate backgrounds by legal domain and examine how court composition conditions their influence. Each additional year as an ICE attorney is associated with a lower relief rate, regardless of court composition. Experience as a nonprofit immigration defense attorney is associated with higher relief rates only where former ICE colleagues are few, fading as their share grows. We interpret this as asymmetric conformity, in which lenient judges in courts dominated by former ICE attorneys are visible and sanctionable outliers while restrictive judges face no comparable cost.
